Synopsis:
    Indonesia's $12.94B national free meal programme continues to generate mass food poisoning outbreaks, with 1,700+ affected in a single week across multiple provinces. Systemic failures — improper food storage, poor preparation timing, and alleged corruption — are undermining the flagship nutrition initiative of President Prabowo. Public satisfaction with the programme is low (only 1/3 satisfied as of July), and a cumulative 50,000 individuals have been affected as of Sept 1. A lawmaker from the opposition characterizes this as a systemic failure rather than isolated incidents.
